main_body: A round leafy tree canopy (green clumps with lighter highlights on the upper right) on a short brown trunk with a small grass patch at the base
top_band: Canopy: the dome of leaves from row 1 down to about row 31 is shaded as a rounded volume, with lighter highlight clumps (L~141 rows 13-14 and 29-30) and darker clumps below. There is no distinct flat top band; the top is the lit upper part of the dome.
evidence: This is an organic tree canopy, a rounded volume with lit upper clumps and a darker underside that casts shade onto the trunk. It has no flat horizontal surfaces to check, and no receding side face. It reads as a normal 3/4 tree like the Beodeul tree references, with a rounded dome over a short trunk. The dark underside of the canopy acts as the shadow where it meets the trunk.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours and a median of 6 colours per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 distinct colours in the references. The canopy has about 5 green steps (dark outline, deep green, mid, light, highlight), but it is built from large blocky clumps with no per-leaf highlights or fine leaf texture, whereas the references have many small leaf clusters. The outline is a dark teal-green tint (#142a2c), so it is tinted and not neutral black (0% neutral). The trunk is a plain two-tone brown stripe with a pattern of alternating rows and little bark detail. The grass patch is simple. Next to the references the piece looks much thinner and flatter, so it fails on density.
